chunks: Al-Baqir and Al-Sadiq, peace be upon them, said:
There is no issue with a blind person leading the prayer if they are satisfied with him and he is the most proficient among them in recitation and the most learned in fiqh.

key_terms.أَفْقَهَهُمْ: the most knowledgeable among them in fiqh
key_terms.رَضُوا: they were satisfied and accepted him
key_terms.قِرَاءَةً: recitation, especially proper recitation relevant to prayer
key_terms.يَؤُمَّ: to lead others in congregational salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can a blind person lead congregational prayer in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a blind person may lead congregational salat (prayer) if the worshippers accept him and he is superior to them in recitation and fiqh. It shows that eligibility for leading prayer depends on religious merit and communal acceptance, not on physical sight.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1108 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) and Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"There is no issue for a blind person to lead the prayer if the people (praying behind him) are satisfied with him and he is the best among them in recitation and the most knowledgeable in religious jurisprudence."
